As home gardens flourish in Toronto once again, the @cityofto is encouraging residents to help us bee pollinator-friendly by: 

1. Cutting turfgrass on lawns when the growth exceeds 20cm 
2. Keeping properties free of prohibited plants that can pose a risk to human health 
3. Steering clear of blocking sidewalks or driver views from plants 
4. Consider replacing turfgrass with native flowering plants to create habitat for pollinators 🌱

To learn more, visit toronto.ca/grassandgardens

Happy gardening! 🌼🐝

While we embrace how far we have come, we must also look in to our past, acknowledge the pain and oppression of Indigenous peoples on which our country is built on, and channel that reflection into continued action on Truth & Reconciliation.

As a land of opportunity and refuge for many, we are incredibly lucky to live in the greatest country on earth. And that greatness exists because of the different cultures and unique backgrounds that make Canada diverse, and our commitment to building a bright future together.

As we celebrate how far we’ve come, let’s recognize the sacrifice of those that have made it possible, and keep creating the  opportunities, reflections, and collaborations for a better future for all that call Canada and Toronto home. 🇨🇦🍁

I visited 444 Lumsden this afternoon to meet with residents following the major flooding incident and to hear their concerns.

TCHC staff have secured hotel accommodation for all affected residents, and staff will be arranging food and school transportation for all families who need it. Staff are working hard to get elevators back online and ensure the safety of all building systems. 

I asked staff and residents to reach out to my office for any additional assistance they need. Together, we will make sure residents are supported through this difficult time.

A serious flooding incident has taken place at the Toronto Community Housing building at 444 Lumsden Avenue. At this time, at least 43 units have been affected. 

Toronto Fire has set up a Command Post on-site and Toronto Community Housing is standing up its Emergency Operations Centre. Right now, they are focused on responding to the immediate needs for all tenants, including shelter, food and water. Any residents who are displaced will have alternate accommodation provided. 

I’ve been in touch directly with the response team, including the Fire Chief, TCHC, Toronto Water and Toronto Emergency Management, to monitor the initial response and offer whatever additional assistance is required. Thank you to all of these teams for your quick response. 

My priority is ensuring that all tenants in the building have access to the resources and support that they need, now and in the days ahead.

Ahead of the Victoria Day weekend, I have worked alongside City of Toronto staff and the Toronto Police to ensure proper community safety measures are in place.

To manage the large crowds expected at Woodbine Beach, a coordinated effort involving Toronto Police, Fire Services, EMS, and City By-law officers will be active throughout the weekend. 

Measures include increased police presence, parking enforcement, extended washroom access, and extra TTC service to accommodate visitors. 

Alcohol, open fires, and personal fireworks remain prohibited on City beaches. 

Hope everyone has a safe and enjoyable Victoria Day weekend!
